solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pester evil European, man not wanted

parts.note: evil means bad

indicators.note: something not wanted is thrown out, so these letters are dropped from the European

parts.note: a German is a European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked European troublemaker is being shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man not wanted' looks like a separate person; it actually says what to drop from the European.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone is to nag or harass them persistently, as the verb with the animal's name means.

clue.text: Meagre bishop, ancient, going empty inside

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: inside means the emptied word is set within the ancient word

parts.note: early can mean ancient, as in early times

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word going is removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: An old, impoverished bishop is getting hollow-cheeked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps G and G from 'going', and 'inside' sets them within EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry and poor like a beggar's lot, the adjective describes something scanty.

clue.text: Man does it differently and prevails

indicators.note: differently means the letters of man does it are to be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A man goes about a task in his own way and wins through.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail over others is to hold control over them, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Registers unfortunate layperson deprived of pay absurdly

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone awry, so the letters of layperson are rearranged once the pay letters are gone

explanation.surface: A luckless member of the public signs up, though deprived of any wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' takes P, A and Y out of LAYPERSON, and 'absurdly' says they come out scattered; the remaining LERSON is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up on a list or course is what both verbs mean, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Heroic every evening following king

indicators.note: following tells us the evening word comes after the king's letter

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
something done every evening happens nightly

explanation.surface: Someone is brave every single evening after the king calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights are the chivalric heroes of romance, so behaving like one is gallant and brave.

clue.text: I'll say clan got animated, looking back to past with fondness

definitions.text: looking back to past with fondness

indicators.note: animated means stirred into lively motion, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone reminisces warmly as the family grows lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful longing for earlier times is what this adverb conveys, matching the fond backward look.

clue.text: Country girl

definitions.meaning: a nation in the Caucasus, or a US state

explanation.surface: A rural young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' reads as one phrase but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a Caucasus nation and a woman's given name.

clue.text: Monster responsible for number of casualties crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the casualty word straddles the river letter

parts.note: the death toll is the number of casualties

explanation.surface: A beast that has killed many people wades over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave-dwelling giant or ugly creature from Scandinavian folklore is a kind of monster.

clue.text: One getting about in city — one known in a play

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the city

parts.note: York is a city in northern England
one is I in Roman numerals
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone travelling around a city turns out to be a famous stage name.
explanation.walkthrough: C is short for circa, Latin for about.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet holds up the jester's skull in Shakespeare's tragedy, so he is a character known from that drama.

clue.text: Player in school having bit of hesitation

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A schoolchild in a play stumbles a little over the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a classroom but a pod of whales, a GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plays, especially video games, is called by this term, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Duke is taking time, admitting no shame

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the time word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A duke takes his time but won't confess to any disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgrace or loss of honour is the meaning of both words, so they are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Indicate "sorry" when going wrong? It's as one decides

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters of indicate sorry go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to apologise when things go awry.
explanation.definitionFit: Left to personal judgement rather than fixed by rule, the adjective means decided at will.

clue.text: Ring American, set aside at first

indicators.note: at first places the set-aside word at the front, ahead of the American

parts.note: to set aside a ruling is to annul it

explanation.surface: Someone telephones an American and puts other matters aside to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry it is the ring-shaped region between two concentric circles.

clue.text: A new well-bred young lady in charge, very kind

parts.note: gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl, used for a posh young woman

explanation.surface: A new debutante takes charge and turns out to be very kind.
explanation.walkthrough: GEL is how a cut-glass British accent says girl, so it means a well-bred young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly goodness of the sort credited to heavenly beings is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Many conspiracies to remove leader

indicators.note: remove leader means take away the first letter of the conspiracies word

parts.note: conspiracies are plots

explanation.surface: Plotters keep scheming to oust the person at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a great many of something is a large number or plenty.

clue.text: Expecting to be ruling alongside president

indicators.note: alongside sets the two pieces next to each other in a row

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to govern side by side with the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who is expecting is carrying a baby, the common euphemism for this condition.

clue.text: Thieves disappear in a set dispersing

indicators.note: in places the disappear word inside the scattered letters
dispersing scatters the letters of a set

parts.note: to leave is to go away, to disappear

explanation.surface: Robbers vanish while a group scatters.
explanation.walkthrough: This is Cockney rhyming slang for thieves. 'dispersing' rearranges A SET, which then wraps round the disappear word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang the phrase stands for burglars and robbers.

clue.text: Dry friend showing cruel aspect

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A dry-witted friend reveals a nasty side.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUT is the label for the driest champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a savage, harsh manner is what the adverb means.

clue.text: Time of year to get sun on street and evidence of freezing

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
ice shows that water has frozen

explanation.surface: Midwinter brings sunshine on the road and frost on the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest or shortest day falls on this date, twice a year, marking the season's turn.

clue.text: Disappointment making one lower

definitions.meaning: an anticlimax or failure to meet hopes
lowering something, as a rope or hem, by releasing it

explanation.surface: A setback that leaves someone feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a disappointment; the verb phrase lowers something gradually.

clue.text: Covering item of furniture when bit of cloth's gone

indicators.note: gone means the small piece is no longer there, removed from the furniture word

parts.note: a chair is an item of furniture

indicators.note: bit of picks only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A seat's upholstery has worn away, leaving a scrap of fabric missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The growth on a head or animal's body acts as a natural coat or covering.

clue.text: Wife with cat, someone evoking pity?

parts.note: to cat is slang for to vomit or retch

explanation.surface: A wife with her cat seems a pitiable figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is not the pet but a slang verb for being sick.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfortunate, miserable person is pitied, which is what this noun names.

clue.text: Punishment changed, cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: amended means changed

explanation.surface: A penalty has been revised and shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword for a fine or penalty, used in English for reparation.

clue.text: Food to stir, mixed with egg in

indicators.note: in puts the egg letter inside the mixed letters
mixed means the letters of to stir are jumbled

parts.note: an egg is O-shaped, so it gives O

explanation.surface: A cook stirs a dish and beats in an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges TO STIR, and 'in' puts the egg's round letter into the middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock is a kind of food.

clue.text: Tot Bill found in wood

parts.note: to tot up gives a sum
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A child named Bill turns up in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub or tree whose timber is used, so its name stands for a kind of wood.

clue.text: Light unit with an orange tinge carried by officer

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the officer's letters

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
amber is a yellowish-orange shade

explanation.surface: A lieutenant carries an orange lamp on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed grid gives LAMBENT, but the clue clearly builds LAMBERT: AMBER held in LT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting engineers measure luminance, the brightness of a surface, with this old unit named after a physicist.

clue.text: Portray me looking unconventional, casual

indicators.note: looking unconventional suggests the letters of portray me appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: An artist asks to be painted in a quirky style.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual work is short-term, not permanent, so the adjectives share that sense.

clue.text: Christmas centred around very short work of fiction

indicators.note: centred around means the festive word is placed around the short piece at its middle

parts.note: Noel is another name for Christmas
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A Christmas story is built around something very brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A book-length prose story is the standard sense of this noun.

clue.text: Carriages with horses for conveying French soldier

indicators.note: conveying means carrying, so the horses word holds the soldier

parts.note: hacks are horses for ordinary riding
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Coaches and horses are laid on to transport a French soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal NEY is the crossword's stock French soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-drawn cabs for hire were called by this name, from the breed of horse that pulled them.

clue.text: Gosh — see Irish jumping into that river!

indicators.note: jumping into means leaping inside the exclamation

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: An onlooker gasps at an Irishman diving into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The MERSEY is the river at Liverpool, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-west English river flows to the sea at Liverpool, an example of a river.
